The image of $\phi^j$ is $\gcd(k^j, m) \cdot \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$. Writing $m = \prod q_i^{e_i}$ and $k = \prod q_i^{c_i} \cdot k'$ (with $\gcd(k', m)=1$):

$$\gcd(k^j, m) = \prod_{q_i \mid m} q_i^{\min(j \cdot c_i,\, e_i)}$$

As $j \to \infty$, this stabilizes at:
$$D = \prod_{\substack{q_i \mid m \\ q_i \mid k}} q_i^{e_i}$$

$$\bigcap_{j=1}^{\infty} \operatorname{Im}(\phi^j) = D \cdot \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$$

$$\sum_{k=1}^{m} m_0(k) = m \prod_{q \mid m} \left(\frac{1}{q} + \frac{(q-1)\cdot q^{v_q(m)}}{q}\right) = m \prod_{q \mid m} \frac{1 + (q-1)\,q^{v_q(m)}}{q}$$
